title: II. Exploring the role of the Crystal Electric Field in the vicinity of a Quantum Critical Point
authors: Julian G. Sereni, Ivan Curlik, Slavo Gabani, Mauro Giovannini
abstract: Very low temperature thermdynamic properties of the Yb$T_4M$ family of compounds are analyzed in a broad range of behavior including a quantum critical point QCP between magnetic and Fermi-liquid ground states GS. Doniach-Lavagna phase diagram limitations are improved by taking into account crystal electric field CEF splittings. The studied alloys: Yb$T_{5-x}M_x$ (with $T$= Ni, Cu, and $M$= Cd, Mg, Pd, Au, Zn, Ag), allow to gain insight into the evolution of the GS behavior undergoing the QCP region as a function of chemical doping as control parameter. Three types of behaviors are recognized in this system: i) a magnetic one, with weak interactions at $T_m\leq 1$\,K and very low Kondo temperature of their respective doublets GS. Between $T_m$ and $T_q\approx 0.3$\,K, quantum fluctuations start to dominate the scenario with the specific heat $C_{4f}/T(T\geq T_q)$ showing $T$ power law dependencies and a very heavy-fermion {\it plateau} below $T_q$. ii) beyond the QCP the typical non-fermi-liquid logarithmic $T$ dependence: $C_{4f}/T \propto \ln(T/T_0)$ and iii) at the non-magnetic limit, the alloys behave as valence-fluctuation systems with $T_K$ overcoming the CEF splitting. With this experimental information, a more realistic phase diagram can be drawn around the QCP where the scenario is dominated by low lying quantum fluctuations, without $C_{4f}/T|_{Lim T\to 0}$ divergences but a clear drop of its value.
summary: This paper investigates the role of Crystal Electric Field splitting in understanding Quantum Critical Points within Yb-based compounds. By analyzing low-temperature specific heat measurements across doping series, the authors refine existing phase diagrams. They conclude that the QCP is better understood as a crossover dominated by quantum fluctuations rather than a singular point defined by diverging thermodynamic quantities.
main_problem: The study explores how Crystal Electric Field (CEF) splitting modifies the understanding of Quantum Critical Points (QCPs) when a system transitions between magnetic and Fermi-liquid ground states.
main_result: The analysis suggests that the QCP region is better described as a crossover dominated by low-lying quantum fluctuations, rather than a singularity characterized by divergences in specific heat measurements.
method: The research analyzes very low temperature thermodynamic properties, particularly the specific heat divided by temperature (C4f/T), across various doping levels within the YbT4M family of compounds.
model_or_system: The physical platform is the YbT4M family of intermetallic compounds. The theoretical framework improves upon the Doniach-Lavagna phase diagram by explicitly incorporating CEF splittings to model the competition between magnetic ordering, Kondo screening, and valence fluctuations.
key_observables: Specific heat divided by temperature (C4f/T), which exhibits power law dependencies, logarithmic divergences ($\propto \ln(T/T_0)$), or near-constant behavior depending on the electronic regime.
important_parameters: The key parameters include the Kondo temperature ($T_K$), the magnetic ordering temperature ($T_m$), and the CEF splitting energy ($\Delta_{	ext{CEF}}$). The doping level acts as a control parameter mapping out different regimes.
main_assumptions: Early models' predictions of divergences at the QCP are revised; instead, the transition is characterized by a clear drop in $C_{4f}/T$ towards zero temperature.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate phase diagrams (e.g., magnetic vs. non-magnetic regions) and plot C4f/T versus temperature for various doped alloys to map out distinct physical regimes.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the low-temperature behavior across three identified regimes—magnetic, non-Fermi liquid, and valence fluctuation—using doping as a tuning parameter to construct a more realistic phase diagram around the QCP.
why_interesting: This work provides detailed experimental evidence on how crystal field effects modify the expected critical behavior near magnetic quantum criticality in heavy fermion systems, offering insights into the nature of quantum fluctuations beyond simple mean-field models.
